reuse.why: All six link handlers reuse the new guards and existing bank lookup and sync helpers, although local unlink cleanup is copied.

duplication.why: Fintegra duplicates the existing link workflow and transaction-download routine, while replacement duplicates unlinkAccount's field-reset block.

placement.why: Link orchestration, provider downloads, endpoint configuration and provider types remain in their established layers.

scope.why: The edits are confined to the requested linking rules, Fintegra integration and associated tests.

maintainability.why: Shared guards centralize the rules, but repeated workflows and a validation-named helper that now mutates accounts make future changes harder to own.

bypasses_abstraction.where: All link handlers use both shared guards and findOrCreateBank; the existing unlinkAccount action includes remote cleanup unsuitable for link transfer.

disguised_duplication.where: linkFintegraAccount condenses the existing providers' create-or-upgrade and sync workflow, and downloadFintegraTransactions reshapes downloadEnableBankingTransactions without sharing its common logic.

abstraction_drift.where: ensureBankAccountIsNotLinked gains replaceExistingLink and a replacement branch that clears another account's link, expanding a refusal guard into a mutating operation; all six link handlers still use it.
